findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'Cape Agulhas', the zoomed-in globe of the Cape cuts to an almost black frame, and the ASTER satellite plate then ramps up over 3 frames. The result is a dark blink at the cut. Every other cut in the segment is clean, so this one stands out as a glitch.
findings.evidence: Detector event E8. Exact-frame mean luma: f24929 32.3, f24930 32.3, f24931 4.2, f24932 15.3, f24933 27.4, f24934 39.2, f24935 41.6. Motion energy at 24931-24934 is 28.4 / 11.1 / 12.1 / 11.9, then 2.9. I viewed 24928-24935 at full rate: 24931 is black with only a faint ghost of the plate.
findings.likely_cause: M2 (the ASTER plate) has fadeIn 0.12, but LM ends exactly at M2's start (LMb = M2a = M.agul - 0.07). film.html draws a fading scene into layerA and composites it at alpha lt/fadeIn over whatever was already drawn that frame. LM is no longer active, so all that is underneath is the #05070D background, and the 'fade' becomes a dip from black. ch4 and ch5b scene B1 avoid this by overlapping the outgoing scene by the fade length (e.g. B1a = A_end - 0.4). M2 is missing that overlap.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch5b.js:700 (LMb = M.agul - 0.07), :734 (M2a = LMb), :755 ({ fadeIn: 0.12 }); compositing in engine/www/film.html:67-71
findings.suggested_fix: Make it a real crossfade. At ch5b.js:700 set LMb = M.agul - 0.07 + 0.12, and at ch5b.js:734 set const M2a = M.agul - 0.07 (instead of = LMb). LM then keeps drawing for the 0.12 s fade; scenes are drawn in t0 order, so LM lands first and M2 composites over it. Alternatively, delete { fadeIn: 0.12 } at :755 for a clean hard cut like the rest of the chapter. Re-render chunk 55 (frames 24750-25199).

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 'IT'S COMPLICATED' globe hard-cuts to the scars globe at almost the same size, the same screen position and the same heading, only tilted 25 deg south. The red Africa/India mass jumps up by about a quarter of the disc in one frame, and the stamp and coin vanish. With the same subject and framing, it reads as a skipped chunk (a jump cut) rather than a new shot.
findings.evidence: E12 strip, plus frames 25517-25520 at 960 px. The disc centre is unchanged and the radius changes about 8% (alt 2.885 -> 3.2). The heading is matched: N1 ends at 0 + 1.2 deg/s x 5.97 s = 7.2 deg, and N2 starts at 8 deg. Only the latitude jumps (-30 -> -55). The other globe-to-globe cuts here (E10, E13, E14) change hemisphere or zoom and read as normal cuts.
findings.likely_cause: N1 and N2 are separate globe shots joined by a plain cut, with keys at lat -30 (end of N1) and lat -55 (start of N2). Everything else in the framing is matched, which is exactly what makes it a jump cut.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the jump with a camera tilt. At ch5b.js:806 change N2's keys to [{ t: N2a, lat: -30, lon: 16, alt: 2.9, heading: 7.2 }, { t: N2a + 0.8, lat: -55, lon: 15, alt: 3.2, heading: 8 }, { t: N2b, lat: -58, lon: 12, alt: 3.1, heading: 8 }]. At :807, make the look a function that eases dim from 0.55 to 0.35 over the same 0.8 s (N1 ends at dim 0.55). Fade the stamp and coin out over N1's last 0.2 s. Re-render chunk 56 (25200-25649).

findings.frames: 24060-24153 (two peninsulas visible while the red copy slides); the white cross-line is visible on the red Baja through 24221
findings.what_viewer_sees: When Baja lights up, the red Baja appears about 270 km south-east of the real one, lying over the Gulf of California and the Sonora coast, while the real unhighlighted peninsula is clearly visible just west of it. findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch5b.js:130-133 (bajaFeat, BAJA_Q, bajaStart), :636-638 (fill and stroke of the moving rings R)

Alternatively, show the start position as a dashed 'ghost' outline and fill only at arrival. For the cross-line, merge the two features once at build time (drop edges shared by both rings, or topojson/d3 merge) and stroke the merged outline instead of each admin ring. Re-render chunks 53-54 (23850-24749).

findings.frames: word 'scars' at about f25494 (over the stamp hold); N2 cut at f25519; scar lines start drawing at f25577
findings.what_viewer_sees: '...they're SCARS from a supercontinent' is heard over the coin and the 'IT'S COMPLICATED' stamp, which holds still for 2.2 s after it lands. The stitched scar lines only start drawing on 'Antarctica', 2.8 s after the word 'scars'.

Add scars: mk('scars', 's095') to M, and at :811 use st = M.scars - 0.1 + i * 0.35, so the three sutures draw across 'scars from a supercontinent that tore apart' and finish by 'Antarctica'. findings.frames: 23926-23950; near standstill 23938-23945 between two moves in the same direction
findings.what_viewer_sees: Right after the cut to the Americas globe, the camera drifts toward Baja, slows to a full stop for about 0.25 s around 'stories', then restarts in the same direction for the long dive into Baja. It reads as a small hesitation in what should be one move.

result.intended_notes:
EVENTS:
- Intended and reading well:
  - E1/E2: the 0.65 s re-layout of the tiles from grid to strip. Tiles cross each other for about 4 frames, but it reads as a shuffle.
  - Hard cuts on narration beats, each within about 0.1 s of its word: E3 (Peninsula), E4, E5 (Florida), E6 (limestone), E7 (West), E9 (compass), E10, E13, E14, E16, E17.
  - E9: the compass pops in with an outBack scale.
  - E11: stamp slam plus a 0.35 s shake.
  - E15: the northern land slams to red in 2 frames on 'lopsided', with an exposure boost.
  - E17/E18: the slice pops in with an outBack overshoot and settles.
  - E19: shutter flash, then the Polaroid develops and the caption wipes in.
- Defects: E8 is a dip-to-black blink (S9-1). E12 reads as a jump cut (S9-2).

CLEAN AT FULL FRAME RATE:
- York and Yucatan needle swings (the yellow-to-white switch mid-swing is fine).
- J push-in and pull-out (the stop is at a natural direction reversal) and the 16-arrow burst.
- Florida swoop.
- The arc and the truck crossing, which lands on 'else'.
- The fly to the Cape. The energy dip mid-flight is low-texture ocean, not a speed change.
- The Good Hope to Agulhas hop.
- M2 Ken Burns. The tip marker math is valid (the image is 1.85:1) and the bottom fill band's colour is stable (max 0.55 per frame).
- Compass spin, settle and ring.
- Coin spin and settle (a 2-frame speed-up at f25444-45 is hidden by the stamp).
- N3 glitch flicker-in and the connecting dots.
- O1, the O2 zoom, O3 arrow and X, and P.
- Smaller, not reported: the J yellow arrowhead appears at the end of its path one frame before the line reaches it (f23749).

CHUNK SEAMS (23850, 24300, 24750, 25200, 25650, 26100): no look change at any of them. Seam diffs are mildly raised (largest at 24300: 1.06 vs 0.13-0.30 for the neighbouring pairs), but the extra difference is spread evenly as edge and texture noise. That is the I-frame refresh of the separately encoded CRF-12 chunk files. Mean RGB is unchanged and the Florida crop is identical. There is no state-dependent rendering of the ch2_sets kind. getSnap (P) is built once per page with an explicit look, and every globe shot here sets its overlay and patch itself.

SAME RUNTIME CAVEAT ELSEWHERE: film.html fades from black when the outgoing scene does not overlap the fadeIn. ch5b.js:202 (B1) overlaps correctly. The other modules' fadeIn scenes (ch3:139/535, ch5a:706/768, ch6:555/591/704) are worth a quick check for that overlap.

TOOLING: tools/grab.py duplicates the first decoded frame (ffmpeg's default constant-frame-rate mode, combined with -ss (f0-0.5)/30). Every label after the first is therefore one frame late: label N shows frame N-1. Verified: the black frame 24931 appears under label 24932. Fix: add '-fps_mode', 'passthrough' to the ffmpeg call at tools/grab.py:26. The pack's sheets and event strips are numbered correctly. I used a fixed copy (review6/s9work/grab2.py), so all frame numbers above are exact.

AUDIO: the README flag at 14:04.36 is real. There is an abrupt drop at 844.36-844.37, the end of s094 'north.'. No visual event coincides with it (the N1 cut is at 844.67). It is outside the animation scope.

findings.frames: 21798-21835 (second planet flip), 21838-21841 (check mark visible), 21842 (hard cut to Pangooy map, E13)
findings.what_viewer_sees: The hamster-wheel gag's payoff misses its line. The planet only finishes flipping back to Antarctica-on-top 0.6 s after 'it was right the first time' has ended, while the narrator is already saying 'And one day'. The yellow check mark then flashes for 4 frames, still scaling up, before a hard cut to the map. It reads as a yellow blink rather than a punchline.
findings.evidence: In timing.json the marker 'first' = 726.61 sits on the word 'time.' (the word 'first' starts at 726.33). The s085 line ends at 727.25. The second flip runs 726.59-727.84 and completes at frame 21835. The check (outBack over 0.3 s from 727.89) is first visible at 21838 at ~30% scale and still growing at 21841, then D ends at Db = 728.05, so the next frame (21842) is the Pangooy map. Stepped 21786-21801 and 21818-21845.
findings.likely_cause: r2a is anchored to M.first (726.61 = 'time.') and run 2 lasts 1.25 s. The tick fires at r2b+0.05, only 0.16 s before the scene end Db = s086.start + 0.4, so the tick and the cut collide.
findings.suggested_fix: At ch5b.js:277 anchor run 2 on the word 'first' and shorten it: const wFirst = C.words('s085').find(w => /^first/i.test(w.w)).start; r2a = wFirst - 0.3, r2b = r2a + 1.0. The flip then runs ~726.03-727.03 and the check lands ~727.08 right after 'time.'. The turn key r2a-0.25 = 725.78 still follows the run-1 idle at 725.55. Optionally set Db = SEG('s086').start + 0.6 at :267 so the check holds about 1 s; scene E's first beat is the splash at 730.0, so nothing is lost.

findings.what_viewer_sees: A same-subject jump cut. The teardrop world map snaps about 20% smaller and re-centres in one frame, every drop jumps to a new size and position, and the five yellow tip arrows vanish instantly. Nothing else changes, so it looks like a glitch rather than an edit.
findings.evidence: Frame 21253 is B1's last frame (view cx 1840, cy 840, zoom 1.1) with the tip arrows at full alpha. Frame 21254 is B2's first frame (cx 1800, cy 880, zoom 0.9) with no arrows. Detector diff 20.4 vs local median 0.14. The 'TEAR-DROP SHAPED' pill had already faded, so the map change is the only thing happening. Viewed 21250-21257 at 960 px.
findings.likely_cause: B1 and B2 are independent scenes with unmatched framings: B1 pushes in to zoom 1.1 while B2 starts at a hard-coded 0.9, and the B1 arrows have no fade-out before B1b.
findings.suggested_fix: Start B2 from B1's end framing and ease out. At :214-216: const kIn = prog(t, B2a, B2a + 0.9, E.inOut); zoom = lerp(1.1, lerp(0.9, 0.97, prog(t, B2a, B2b)), kIn) * (1 - 0.06*Math.sin(Math.PI*flipP)); drawEE(ctx, { cx: lerp(1840, 1800, kIn), cy: lerp(840, 880, kIn), zoom }, lerp(0.5, 0.48, kIn)). The ease finishes by 709.35, long before the flip at 712.67. At :199-200 multiply the arrow alpha by (1 - prog(t, B1b - 0.35, B1b)).

findings.what_viewer_sees: On the 'Tuesday, 9:00 a.m.' calendar card, the red '1,786,379 A.D.' runs off the card's right edge onto the dark map, and the comma after 'A.M.' hangs on the edge, for the whole ~4.5 s hold.
findings.evidence: Full-res crop of 22100: the 'D.' ends ~25 px beyond the card's right edge. The card is cw = 650 and the text starts at x = 230 at 54 px (line 1) and 62 px (line 2).
findings.likely_cause: The card width is hard-coded at 650 and was never fitted to the two text lines at their font sizes.
findings.suggested_fix: Fit text to card. Either drop the sizes to 48 (label line) and 54 (date line), which leaves ~30 px margin, or measure both lines with the same font settings F.text uses and set cw = 230 + maxWidth + 48. If the card widens, slide it to W - cw - 70 instead of 1150 and check it doesn't overlap the blob (right edge ~x 1100).

findings.frames: 23446-23472 (continues past the segment end until each tile's north swing, ~783.2+); full-res check at 23468
findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'Not everything drips', 12 needles grow in. The four bottom-row needles (Cape York, Yucatán, Jutland, Taymyr) point straight down from near the tile bottoms and stick 60-75 px out below the tile frames into the empty gutter. The other eight stay inside their tiles.
findings.evidence: Full-res 23468: the arrowheads of the bottom row sit at y≈995-1010 while the tile bottoms are at ≈938; the needles cross the tile borders. Stepped 23434-23449: they grow from 23446.
findings.likely_cause: For north tiles the pre-swing needle points straight down (ang = PI/2) from s.b with the full base-to-tip length. Because these peninsulas point north, the base is near the bottom of the tile, so a needle of that length overshoots the tile. Needles are drawn after the tile clip is restored.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the south-pointing needle inside the tile and grow it to full length as it swings. After computing by and L: const room = h / 2 - 16 - by; const Ls = Math.min(L, Math.max(24, room)); const Ld = s.north ? lerp(Ls, L, clamp(q)) : L; then use Ld in U.arrow. Hoist q out of the if-block so it is in scope here.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Just before the googly eyes pop, the whole merged 'Pangooy' blob outline twitches in a single frame: the top-left lobe flattens and the rim jumps ~10-15 px. It then keeps jiggling.
findings.evidence: Mean abs diff in the blob region is ≈1.0 per frame for 21970-21977, then 4.1 for 21977->21978, then 2.4 and 2.0. The amplified diff shows a thick band all round the outline. d(21977,21979) = 4.85, so this is a step change, not a one-frame outlier.
findings.likely_cause: The extra wobble (0.03 + 0.03*exp(-2*lt)) switches on at full strength when lt crosses 0. wob jumps 0.012 -> 0.070, and dropPts scales every outline radius by up to ±wob.
findings.suggested_fix: Ramp the extra wobble in: wob = 0.012 + 0.07*Math.sin(Math.PI*p) + (lt > 0 ? (0.03 + 0.03*Math.exp(-2*lt)) * prog(lt, 0, 0.18, E.out) : 0).

findings.what_viewer_sees: The vertical yellow split-screen divider keeps running to the bottom after the bracket draws. It crosses the bracket bar like a cross-hair and shows through the 'JOHN C. HOLDEN' name pill, right through the 'C.'.
findings.evidence: Full-res 22436: the 4 px divider (x 958-962, y 120-920) crosses the bracket bar at y≈776, is visible through the semi-transparent pill between 'C.' and 'HOLDEN', and continues below it.
findings.likely_cause: The divider is drawn at full height (800*dv) for the whole scene, and the name pill is placed on the same vertical axis with a translucent fill.
findings.suggested_fix: Retract the divider to the top of the bracket legs as the bracket draws: const dvH = lerp(800, (Py + PH + 22) - 130, prog(t, M.apart2 - 0.1, M.apart2 + 0.35, E.inOut)); ctx.fillRect(958, 120, 4, dvH * dv). Alternatively give the pill an opaque fill.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Between the split-screen and the 'DIETZ & HOLDEN' reference card there is one frame of almost empty dark desk, a brief dark blink before the card slams down from the top. The slam itself is designed.
findings.evidence: In 22445 only a sliver of the card is visible at the top edge. The card starts at y = -500, so the first outExpo frame (p≈0.03) puts its centre at ≈-301, off-screen. 22446 shows a quarter of the card and 22447 half.
findings.likely_cause: The slide-in starts fully off-screen exactly on the cut frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the card already entering on the cut frame: y = lerp(-220, 560, ip) + lerp(0, 40, push), so the lower ~40% of the card is visible on frame 1. Alternatively shift the ease earlier: ip = prog(t, G1a - 0.04, G1a + 0.5, E.outExpo).

findings.frames: 23127 (detach), 23132-23134 (drop passes through puddle), 23135 (gone out of the inset), 23139-23140 (puddle starts to swell)
findings.what_viewer_sees: In the honey-spoon inset the falling drop goes straight through the puddle and out of the bottom of the box. The puddle only swells about 0.17 s later, so the splash looks disconnected.
findings.evidence: Inset crops 23125-23140 at full resolution: the drop reaches the puddle at 23132, overlaps it at 23133-23134 and has left the inset by 23135. The puddle is unchanged until 23139.
findings.likely_cause: The fall is coded as 260 px over 0.42 s, but the puddle is only ~62 px below the drop's start (y0+h-24 = 566 vs sy+226 = 504). The puddle growth and the pop_ui cue wait for detach+0.4/0.42.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the drop land on the puddle when it reacts: const land = (y0 + h - 24) - (sy + 226); const fp = clamp((t - detach) / 0.25); fy = sy + 226 + land * fp * fp; draw only while fp < 1. Set pud = prog(t, detach + 0.24, detach + 0.54, E.outBack) and move cue(detach + 0.42, 'pop_ui') to detach + 0.25.

findings.what_viewer_sees: For the first ~1.4 s of the Nevada cross-section, a ghostly white oval floats in the brown crust above the still-small cold drip. It is the drip's highlight, detached from the drip, and it later slides into the bulb.
findings.evidence: In 22912 and 22935 a ~24x44 px white oval sits 40-60 px above the drip's top inside the crust. By 22958 it is inside the bulb.
findings.likely_cause: The highlight is placed at CRUST + L - 80. While L < ~100, at the start of the inOut growth from L = 44, that is above the drip's top edge (CRUST+4).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the highlight inside the bulb and fade it in: const hy = CRUST + 4 + Math.max(L - 80, L * 0.65); ctx.globalAlpha = clamp((L - 70) / 60); then draw the ellipse at (BX - 20, hy) and restore alpha.

result.intended_notes:
I found 9 problems in S8: four major (S8-1 to S8-4) and five minor (S8-5 to S8-9). Detector events: 21 of 23 are designed and read well. E1 (the module cut, then the 1976 paper whips in), E2 (push-in slam on 'Holden'), E3/E4 (paper exit crossfading into the teardrop map), E6 (cyan drop falling on 'down', visible ~12 frames), E7/E8 (the 180° map flip on 'upside down'; it peaks at ~24°/frame but is smooth and reads as a deliberate whip), E9 (JOKE tag dropping on its string), E10 (cut to the empty photo frame drawing on), E11 (end of the photo rotation and crossfade), E12, E14 (calendar card slam), E15/E16 (twist beat: cut to the empty field, the divider grows under a shake, both panels slam in), E18, E19 (1973 DRIP sheet slam, a designed 1-s callback), E20, E21, E22 (honey inset pop) and E23 are all designed. E23 is a deliberate ~1.1 s dark 'scan' beat; the cyan scan line is clearly visible at full resolution. E5 is defect S8-2. E17 is a designed slam but has the empty first frame in S8-7. E13 is a fine cut in itself, but it truncates the check mark in S8-1.

Clean stretches, stepped at full frame rate:
- A: slide-in, byline ring draw-on, push and sharpen, exit.
- B1: drop pop-in and tip arrows on 'direction'.
- B2: the drop fall, flip and JOKE tag.
- C: frame draw-on, 'SHOT WITH ANTARCTICA ON TOP' pill on 'Antarctica', ring on 'on top', rotation and crossfade on 'flipped'.
- D: run 1, the 180° turnaround (21790-21797, quick but clean), both run-to-idle blends. No T-pose, foot pops or snaps.
- E: slosh and merge, eyes on 'Pangooy', bell shake and clock spin on 'time zone'.
- F: labels on 'earlier' and 'real', the trails, the bracket on 'apart'.
- G1: highlighter on 'cited'.
- G2: point glow, three dotted tracks on 'punchline', ring flare on 'answer'.
- H2: globe dive with the marker on 'real drips'.
- H3: drip growth, 'ANTI-DRIP' on the word, push-in.
- I: tiles snap in on 'part'; needles start on 'drips'.

Every visual lands within 0.15 s of its word except D (S8-1).

Chunk seams 21150, 21600, 22050, 22500, 22950 and 23400 show no look change. The frame differences at 21600 and 23400 are 4-9x their neighbours, but they are diffuse x264 keyframe requantisation: mean RGB shift under 0.1 and no edge or colour shift. There is no repeat of the globe-material issue here; no seam falls inside a three.js shot.

Tool bug affecting every segment: tools/grab.py tile labels are +1 frame off after the first tile. The -0.5-frame seek makes ffmpeg's CFR output duplicate the first decoded frame, so the tile labelled N shows frame N-1. Fix: add '-fps_mode passthrough' to its ffmpeg call. All frame numbers here come from a corrected copy (review6/s8work/grab2.py), validated against code cut times (scene C ends at 723.75, so the first planet frame is 21713).

Audio flags:
- 12:03.50 is real. In audio/vo/vo_proc.wav the final 't' burst of 'flipped.' (~-16 dB at 723.49) drops to digital silence within ~15 ms at 723.51, the s084 segment end, so the consonant is clipped with a click. This is audio (VO assembly), not animation; suggested fix: extend that segment's tail by ~60 ms with a short fade.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In gag 10a the Explorer runs sideways across the tiny planet, but his legs strafe the opposite way to his travel (a moonwalk). The grounded foot slides along with the body instead of planting, so the whole run looks like ice-skating.
findings.evidence: FK of models/adventurer.glb (script review6/s10work/glb/fk.py). Run_Left planted feet move -3.0 model units/s in x, so the clip travels +x: the character's left, which is screen-right for this camera-facing hero. Run_Right is the mirror (+3.0). The code moves him to screen-left (x 0 to -1.05) while playing Run_Left, and to screen-right (-1.05 to +1.0) while playing Run_Right. In /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/runL28024_8x1_c.jpg the grounded right foot travels left with the body over 28028-28031 instead of staying put; runfeet28060_12x1_c.jpg shows the same in reverse.
findings.likely_cause: The strafe clips are assigned by screen direction, but Quaternius Run_Left/Run_Right are named from the character's point of view, and he faces the camera (ry=0). There is also a speed mismatch: the clip's natural speed is about 1.65 world u/s at scale 0.55, while the Run_Right path peaks at about 3.4 u/s (2.05 u in 0.95 s, inOutSine).
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:442 (hero.play timeline) and ch6.js:447-450 (heroX run segments)
findings.suggested_fix: Swap the clips: hero.play(runL0, 'Run_Right', ...)... .play(runR0, 'Run_Left', ...). Then match speed: for the second run use a near-linear path (short ease in/out) and/or { speed: ~1.6 } on the clip, or lengthen runR1-runR0 to about 1.3 s, so the planted foot stays still relative to the planet.

findings.what_viewer_sees: After the second run the Explorer stands in Idle and glides back toward centre by about 150-200 px over 1.3 s with his feet still. He straightens up from his lean while drifting, as if on a conveyor, and the comment bubble drifts with him.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/glideB28098_12x4_c.jpg: the hero is at about x=1305 at 28098 and about x=1100 at 28134 in the idle pose, with no steps.
findings.likely_cause: heroX lerps 1.0 to 0.35 between runR1+0.3 and runR1+1.6 while the clip timeline plays 'Idle' from runR1, so root translation has no locomotion.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:451 (return lerp(1.0, 0.35, prog(t, runR1 + 0.3, runR1 + 1.6, E.inOutSine))) with ch6.js:442
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the root where the run ended (return 1.0) and re-centre by easing the camera target/look instead, or schedule a locomotion clip for the drift. For example, hero.play(runR1 + 0.25, 'Run_Right' (screen-left for him) or a 'Walk' turned with ry toward -x, {speed ≈ 0.7}) and then 'Idle' at runR1 + 1.6, so the feet plant.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Three transitions blink to black: gag 10a to the splash map, the splash map to the heat globe, and the drip globe to the Bacon desk. A full-brightness picture is replaced by a black frame, and the new shot then fades up over about 0.3 s. There is no fade-out, so it reads as a dropout or blink rather than a crossfade.
findings.evidence: Mean luminance per frame: 25.1 -> 2.1 at 28137, then a linear ramp to 17.3 at 28146. Likewise 23.5 -> 1.8 at 28317 (ramp to 28326) and 16.5 -> 2.2 at 28891 (ramp to 28898). Detector events E13, E17 and E25 show pure-black event frames; E14 is the end of the first ramp.
findings.likely_cause: These base scenes are declared with { fadeIn: 0.3 / 0.3 / 0.25 }. film.html blends a fadeIn scene over whatever is below it (alpha = lt/fadeIn, so 0 on the first frame). But each outgoing base scene ends exactly at the incoming t0 (gag 10a ends at GA1 = SP0, splash at SP1 = HT0, drip globe at D1 = BC0), so the fade happens over the black safety-net background. ENGINE.md says to keep the outgoing scene running until the incoming fade ends.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:481 (base(GA0, GA1)), ch6.js:532 (base(SP0, SP1)), ch6.js:664 (base(D0, D1)); fadeIn at ch6.js:555, 591, 704
findings.suggested_fix: Overlap the outgoing scenes by the fade length: base(GA0, GA1 + 0.3, ...), base(SP0, SP1 + 0.3, ...), base(D0, D1 + 0.25, ...). None of the pairs share globe or overlay state: 3D stage to 2D, 2D to fut.draw, globe to 2D. Alternatively drop the three fadeIn options for clean cuts.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'shot.', when the blank film frame turns live, the whole filmstrip snaps about 6% smaller in one frame. The scroll also stops dead from 22 px/frame. The push-in then restarts from scratch and creeps for about 0.4 s before whooshing into the hole, so the beat reads as a hiccup instead of one continuous push.
findings.evidence: Sprocket pitch is 74 px in 29458-29463 and 70 px from 29464. The top sprocket row moves from y 310-332 to 322-343 and the bottom from 747-769 to 736-757. Horizontal shift is -22 px/frame up to 29463 and 0 from 29464 to 29465. See /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/snapzoom29462_4x1.jpg. Detector E32 (motion_stop at 29465) marks the same moment.
findings.likely_cause: The pre-live zoom ends at 1 + 0.06 = 1.06, but the live branch restarts at lerp(1, ..., inExpo(0)) = 1.0. tt = min(t, M.shot - 0.05) also freezes a linear scroll (V2*(M.frame - tt)) with no deceleration.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the live zoom where the pre-live one ends: lerp(1.06, W / FW * 1.1, prog(t, M.shot - 0.05, M.shot + 0.7, inExpo)). Make BLANK_I arrive centred and at rest at TF = M.shot - 0.05: V2 = (BLANK_I - TODAY_I) * PITCH / (TF - M.frame), and replace the linear scroll term with a curve that decelerates to zero over the last ~0.6 s (quadratic ease-out, distance preserved).

findings.likely_cause: s097 draws the ridge at alpha 1 - 0.4*prog(...) = 0.6 by A1. s098 draws drawRidge(ctx, t, fa) with fa starting at 1. s098's globe() also passes ovAlpha 0 and overlay null (s097 had COLD at 0.12) and does not continue the 0.18-alpha drip arcs. The camera also changes from moving to starting at rest (alt about 0.914 to 0.9).
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:322 and ch6.js:325 (s098 base) vs ch6.js:286-288 (s097)
findings.suggested_fix: In s098 use drawRidge(ctx, t, 0.6 * fa). Keep the overlay fading: globe(ctx, camB(t), {..., ovAlpha: 0.12 * fa}, fa > 0 ? COLD : null). Add drawArcs(ctx, t, 0, { full: true, alpha: 0.18 * fa }) while fa > 0.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 'supercontinent will form' globe spin turns 24-38° per frame at its peak. Each frame shows a different face of the Earth (Asia, India, Middle East, Europe/Africa, Atlantic, North America, Pacific within 10 frames), so at speed it strobes and flickers rather than reading as a spin.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Audio, not picture: right after 'Amasia.' a short breath or mouth noise starts and is chopped off, which can be heard as a small click.

findings.what_viewer_sees: During the 'UNDER 1 IN 10 -> 6' countdown, the whole line jumps about 25 px sideways when 10 becomes 9.
findings.evidence: Text extent is x 1212..1747 at 28465 and 1237..1722 at 28466; widths stay equal for 9/8/7/6. See num28462_16x1_c.jpg in review6/grab_s10.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The four tiles settle into the filmstrip, ending with a slight rightward drift, then come to rest. On the next frame the strip is already scrolling left at full speed, a visible hitch with a direction reversal.
findings.evidence: Cross-correlation shift per frame: +2, +9, +4, +2, +1, 0 (28691-28696), then -3 (28697), then a constant -13 px/frame from 28698. Detector E23 marks this motion_start.
findings.likely_cause: The scroll is a linear term -V1*max(0, t - (M.wins + 0.55)) that starts at full speed the moment the inOutExpo morph ends.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace max(0, u) with an eased ramp, e.g. ramp = u => u <= 0 ? 0 : u < 0.4 ? u*u/0.8 : u - 0.2, and start it slightly earlier (M.wins + 0.4) so it accelerates under the tail of the morph.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'one frame of a very slow movie' the strip of map frames pans at about 666 px/s (22 px per frame). The high-contrast sprocket holes and globes judder or strobe at 30 fps, and the highlighted TODAY frame slides off within about 1.5 s.
findings.evidence: Measured a constant -22 px/frame for 29401-29409 by cross-correlation, and sprocket-row offsets of -22/-23 px per frame at 29459-29463. Sprocket pitch is 70-74 px, so each step is about 1/3 pitch.
findings.likely_cause: V2 = 5 frames * 690 px / (M.shot - M.frame = 5.18 s) is about 666 px/s, well above the speed at which a 30p pan of fine detail looks smooth.
findings.suggested_fix: Lower the pan speed: put the blank frame 3-4 frames after TODAY instead of 5, or reduce PITCH while sZ = 1. Alternatively soften the sprocket pattern during the scroll (lower alpha or a 2-3 px horizontal smear).

findings.what_viewer_sees: At the end of the zoom into the live frame, a white vertical line (the hole's border) flashes at the left edge of the screen for 2 frames, then vanishes at the cut to the Afar scene.
findings.evidence: In the left 80 px the brightest column is 88 at x=33 (29486) and 82.7 at x=12 (29487), against a median of about 1.5; it drops to 2.2 at 29488. See leftedge29484_5x1_c.jpg in review6/grab_s10.
findings.likely_cause: The hole is centred at fxB = fX(9, M.shot - 0.05) ≈ 993 px rather than 960 because of the early freeze. The final zoom W/FW*1.02 (≈3.26) only just exceeds the frame width, so the 3*zoom px border strokeRect sits on the left edge until FS1.
findings.suggested_fix: With the S10-4 fix the hole is centred. Also raise the end zoom to about W/FW*1.1, or fade the border with ctx.globalAlpha = 0.5 * (1 - prog(zoom, 1.6, 2.6)).

findings.what_viewer_sees: The glowing sparks along the three Afar rift arms all pop on at full brightness in one frame. They then hop forward in jumps of about 25-35 px roughly every 6 frames, ticking along rather than flowing, for the rest of the film including the end screen.
findings.evidence: Spark peaks on the Gulf of Aden arm: x 1151/1293/1493 for 29640-29645, 1166/1316/1528 for 29646-29651, then 1191/1348/1563 from 29652. See /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/sparkstep29643_12x1_c.jpg; the pop-in is visible at 29568 in t29502_24x3.jpg.
findings.likely_cause: Each spark uses q = P[floor(u*(P.length-1))] with no interpolation between densified points, so a ~25-point arm gives one step every ~0.23 s. All sparks start at full alpha when cp >= 1, and u % 1 makes them teleport from the arm end back to the junction.
findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate: f = u*(P.length-1), i0 = floor(f), i1 = min(i0+1, P.length-1), q = lerp(P[i0], P[i1], f - i0). Scale spark alpha by prog(t, M.cracks + 0.9, M.cracks + 1.3) * Math.sin(Math.PI * u) so they fade in and never visibly wrap.

result.intended_notes:
Intended and reads fine:
- E1: chapter cut, with the card fading in over the bright globe.
- E2: hard cut to the 4-tile grid on 'four main models'. The '?' marks don't carry over exactly, which is acceptable.
- E3-E11: tile expand and shrink snap zooms (inOutExpo 0.5-0.55 s, consistent across all four models). Tile-to-live handovers at 26808, 27097 and 27384 are seamless; the only exception is the Aurica glow (S10-8).
- E12: gag start.
- E15/E16: the 0.58 s Tuesday-card callback flash.
- E18/E26: counter rolls, landing just before 'sixth' and 'ago'.
- E19, E20, E27, E28, E29: hard cuts on sentence starts.
- E21/E22: grid-to-strip shuffle; tiles 1 and 2 briefly cross, acceptable.
- E24: torn halves exit.
- E30: Gondwana snap.

Defective events:
- E13, E14, E17, E25: S10-3.
- E23: S10-10.
- E32: S10-4.
- Missed by the detectors: S10-1, S10-2, S10-5, S10-6, S10-8, S10-11, S10-12, S10-13.

Chunk starts 26550, 27000, 27450, 27900, 28350, 28800, 29250, 29700 and 30150 show no look change. 29700 and 30150 carry only codec GOP noise: mean |d| 1.2/0.9 in the source chunk files, no shift, gain or offset, R² ≈ 0. In code, globe() resets every uniform fut.draw touches, and the STILLS/HOLD/HEATHOLD/AFHOLD/PSTILLS caches are deterministic, so nothing like the 5:45 needsUpdate bug exists in ch6.

Clean stretches:
- s097 ridge draw, 1620 pill (rides off-frame with the camera as a world pin) and bus drop.
- Proxima, Novopangaea, Amasia and Aurica plate motion, arrows, impacts and holds.
- AU+RICA label assembly.
- Splash convergence.
- Heat build.
- Gag 10b faint: the Death clip lands on 'Reminder', with no T-pose or snapping.
- Tear, drip globe and fingerprint arcs.
- Bacon counter, capes globe, p.246 underlines and gold.
- Gondwana snap with the waving Explorer and porch light.
- Afar fly-in and crack draw-on.
- End screen. The last frame (30328) is live, not black.

Narration sync is within about 0.3 s throughout. The QC 'static' stretches 944.4-948.5 and 958.7-963.0 carry the heat build, a slow zoom and the tip highlights, so they are acceptable holds.
